build: Software Projects disk, alternate D64 with LA–LJ files

extra: Scene bytes copied by the runtime loader
Tail of the file loaded at $8010, role unresolved

comments.text: The first copied byte in the scene record is $06. The caller starts executing one byte later.

Save the caller stack pointer and scan the embedded source at $D010 again using escape $54. Replace the disk-load picture with that decoded image, then transform the glyph data at $7E00 and $7F00 for the second descent.
Scan the original staged bytes at $D010 with I/O banked out to find the END OF CODE marker before reusing the first platform picture.
Zero byte between the jump back to the marker scan and the branch destination that sets up decoding.
Point output to $4000 and input to the page after the marker. Save the stream pointer at $2D70/$2D71, then call the shared decoder and transform the glyph bytes in the final two pages.

Restore the saved stack, initialize the raster and character display, clear the scene variables and alternate synthetic up and right inputs until Dirk reaches X=$40. Then poll scene routines until $25 is set.
Run the fire and launch update when $2D5F is nonzero. Return immediately while the enable byte is clear.

From idle, an active-low fire press resets the frame counter and invokes the launch position test. During motion, select the four-piece pose, apply the vertical displacement and move left or right until the frame count reaches $11.
Select the matrix at $4400, draw a nine-row overlay, rebuild its colours and interleave three timer waits with movement updates.
Select the matrix at $4800, apply the three-by-seven patch from $2BD6, service movement during three timer waits and restore the decoded matrices.
Read the joystick and return during the fire arc. Otherwise clear $2D61 and decrement $2904, entering the movement logic when it expires.
Toggle between the sprite pose banks and select the base frame index. Test active-low up, down and horizontal input and use the corresponding four-piece frame tables.
When $2B26 is clear, update the launch position test. Restart the scene through $2D72 and $1EB0 if fire state $2B28 and countdown $2D5E are both zero and the test flag is negative.
At phase zero clear selected character codes from four rows at $4118, then enter the restart sequence. At phase one request sound $88 when $2D57 is in the range $F6–$F9.
Compare the Y of sprite 2 with the interval $57–$6D and combine its row offset with its low X relative to $80. Write the launch displacement and clear $2D53 for the accepted positions.
Set $2D53 to $FF to mark a failed launch position test.
While $2B8A is active, inspect the collision result and update the two extra sprites. Use the low two raster bits to select positions and pointers and service the visibility countdown.
Decrement a nonnegative countdown at $2B8D and toggle the enable bit for sprite 4. A negative countdown branches into the following update.
Save the direction flag from A at $03EF, make repeated calls to the shared updater at $16AD, and enable sprites 0–4 for the first phase of the event.
Count through the event delays at $2B8E–$2B94. Change the extra sprite frames and enables, schedule sound $82 and finish by clearing $2B95 and reinitializing the event counters.
Use $2B96 to select a diagonal two-pixel shift. Update group Y through sprite 0 and use the shared left or right shift for its X coordinates.
Seed the sprite event phase counters at $2B8D–$2B94 and reset the alternating frame flag.

Check the active transition and collision state. On the route through $25CF, switch between the prepared screen matrices, apply transition character patches and interleave movement updates with CIA2 waits.

Use the current matrix phase and the launch flag at $2D5E to select a screen transition or service the fire-triggered movement. After the movement frame counter reaches $11, use the position test at $2321 to select the follow-up animation.
Return opcode following the jump back to the scene initializer and preceding the independent arc routine.
Subtract the signed vertical delta for frame X and adjust it by one pixel according to the position test. Set the other sprite coordinates and move X three times in the direction selected by $2B29.
When $2D62 is active, service the arc and position logic. If the position test succeeds and low X is below $14, clear the transition flag and mark the scene as complete through $25.
Select a quartet from $2B5B or $2B63 using the direction state and whether the frame is between 4 and 12. Use $03EF for orientation and install the result in sprite pointers 0–3.
Clear ten rows of nineteen cells starting at $4173. Draw the ten-row character overlay from $2CE0 at $414B, advancing on $FF or after eighteen cells and setting colours from $7700.
The saved pose base index and its movement delay. $214A resets the delay and updates the index at $2903.
Copy eight sprite pointers and eight bytes at $43D6 from the first display matrix to the other two. Tick the phase counters and service the delay at $2B24 when $2B88 is active.
Add $2D64 to sprite 0 low X and copy the result to sprites 0–3. On carry set their high-X bits. Preserve A.
Subtract $2D64 from sprite 0 low X and copy the result to sprites 0–3. On borrow clear their high-X bits. Preserve A.

Save the eight sprite pointer bytes, then decode from the saved picture stream into $4000 through $4BFF. In the repeated-byte path restore the pointers for all three screen matrices when the output crosses a page boundary.
Continue decoding below page $4C. At $4C or above, select screen page $40 and colour table page $77, then rebuild colour RAM.
Set up a fifteen-cell by nine-row overlay from $2BA9 at $4050 and corresponding colour RAM at $D850.
Set the source row stride to one plus the maximum column index at $03, then enter the compositor.
Walk each source row backward. Write character 0, 2 or $3C and above to the destination with colour from $7700. Skip the other codes and advance both destination rows by forty cells.
Compute a cell address from Dirk's sprite position and compare the corresponding character in all three matrices. Store the shared character in $2D63 or use the fallback value $32 when they differ.
Record character code $32 in $2D63 when the sampled screen cells disagree or the position is beyond the low-X cutoff.
The handler at $2905 decrements this byte while $2B88 is set. At zero it reloads 7 and advances the matrix selector.
Screen page bits for the timed matrix change. The handler adds $10 and wraps at $30 before combining the selector with $0F for $D018.
When zero, the logic at $22B2 checks the launch position and whether the launch state requires a restart.
A zero byte between the launch timeout gate and the fire-arc flag in the scene record.
Initialized to zero. The fire routine at $1FDB tests this byte before starting a launch and writes it as the launch advances.
Direction code written by the movement paths and read by the arc and launch pose selectors.
The movement and restart routines toggle bit 2 to select between two four-sprite poses.
Four pointers for the movement path indexed at $227E and $2291. The renderer stores them into sprite pointers 0–3.
Four companion pointers indexed at $226B and $22A4 for the other movement paths.
Eight pointers for the normal movement update at $214A. It switches between the two groups of four by toggling bit 2 of the pose index.
Eight launch pose pointers for the direction cases that read $2B5B in the routine at $2823.
Eight launch pose pointers for the other direction cases. The runtime starts at index 3 or 7 and writes the selected quartet backwards.
Eight pose pointers used to alternate quartets during the wait loop at $2D7B.
Four consecutive VIC pointers $88–$8B installed in sprites 0–3 for the first strip of the exit animation.
Three pairs of pointers, $8C/$8D through $90/$91, installed in sprites 0 and 1 between successive calls to the diagonal movement routine.
Adjacent pointers $92 and $93 used for the two expanded frames displayed with timed waits.
Two groups of four pointers installed in sprite slots 4–7 at $4FFC before the waits at $2EED and $2F02.
Pointer $9C for the single sprite placed at X=$9C and Y=$8F late in the failure animation.
Enables the matrix cycle in the raster handler. The failure and restart paths clear it before switching matrices.
Countdown adjusted by the extra sprite update at $239B and initialized again by the follow-up at $26FF.
Nonzero enables the update for the extra sprite pair at $2368. Transition paths decrement it as they advance.
Counter initialized to $3C before play. The sprite-pair event updates it at $2388 and $2390.
Countdown decremented at $23AC after the pair-event state check.
Timing bytes through $2B94 for the extra sprite animation. The initializer at $2562 seeds them for the visibility and phase tests at $2445 and $2477.
The pair event at $2380 tests and decrements this byte before updating the extra sprites, and its final phase clears it.
Direction saved at $23B4 and read at $2517 to choose the diagonal displacement during the pair event.
A zero byte between the diagonal direction and the alternating frame flag.
The event at $24BB toggles the extra sprite's frame flag and the initializer at $2588 clears it.
Four groups of four VIC coordinate bytes for sprites 4 and 5. The low two raster bits select a group at $23AF.
Nine rows of fifteen character codes used by $2A2D. The first row lands at $4050 and each successive row advances forty destination cells.
Nine rows of fourteen source character codes for the alternate matrix at $4400. The compositor looks up each copied cell in the colour table at $7700.
Twenty-one additional cell codes after the 126 read by the middle overlay copier. They match the first descent bytes at $2C82–$2C96.
Three rows of seven character codes starting at $2CC3, loaded at $2619 for a patch beginning at $4A0D.
Character copied to $47A2 by the transition at $25F5, with colour 6 written to the corresponding colour RAM cell.
Zero cell code between the two transition characters read directly at $25EA and $25F5. The equivalent byte is $2CAD in the first descent.
Character copied to $47CA by the transition at $25EA, with colour 5 written to the corresponding colour RAM cell.
Five cell codes after the second transition character and before the ten-row overlay. They match the first descent bytes at $2CAF–$2CB3.
Ten rows of character codes for the overlay drawn at $414B by $2894. A row ends on $FF or after eighteen cells.
Eighteen cell codes after the ten consumed rows and before the displacement table. They match the first descent bytes at $2D03–$2D14.
Seventeen signed vertical deltas indexed by the launch frame. The motion routine subtracts the delta from low Y, so positive values move up and negative values move down.
Index into the signed displacement table at $2D41 and the pose tables used by $2823.
The position test clears this flag on acceptance and writes $FF on rejection. Arc updates test its sign before applying their Y correction.
Reset with the scene and decremented at $1FFC during the fire update.
The fire arc checks this byte before changing matrices and decrements it on the return from the far matrix.
The position test updates this byte. Arc movement tests its sign when deciding whether to advance the transition or apply a correction.
The raster handler decrements this byte and decrements $2D58 whenever it reaches zero. The position logic also compares it against the sound timing interval.
The high byte decremented through $2D57 in the raster handler, also used by the scene's position and transition checks.
Initialized to 6 at scene reset. Updated by the fire and matrix transition paths.
Scene state bytes through $2D62 for the matrix transition and fire or movement updates. The update at $258C is gated by $2D60 and reads $2D5A and $2D5E before changing the display.
Character shared by the collision samples from the three matrices, or $32 when they disagree.
Low X increment or decrement used by the two four-sprite group movement routines.
Eight bytes saved from the main matrix by $2993 and restored during picture decoding to keep the sprite images selected.
Seeded with 3 at scene reset. The launch update copies it to the countdown at $2D5D on expiry.
The overlay compositor decrements the source column while incrementing the destination column at $2D6F.
Low and high source bytes saved after locating the embedded picture. The matrix decoder reloads them into $2A/$2B.
Clear the pending sound effect and cycle four sprite pointers over ten CIA2 waits. Select the fourth display matrix and its colour table for the follow-on animation.
Repeat twenty delay calls while decrementing sprite 0 X and incrementing its Y. Reposition the other three pieces after each step.
Clear the scene sound request, display the fourth matrix and sequence sprites 4–7 through grouped and single frames. Use CIA2 waits between changes and finish by enabling sprites 0–3 again.
Copy sprite 0 low X to sprites 1–3. Give sprite 1 the same Y as sprite 0 and sprites 2 and 3 a Y value $15 greater.
This scene record ends with the eleven byte marker copied by the unpacker at $0DDE.
The second descent rewrites these 512 bytes of the shared character set using $170F. The remaining picture bytes $4000–$7DFF match the first descent before play.
A 107-byte slice of the weapon overlay sprite records, matching $309C–$3106 in the Weapons Room snapshot. It begins at record 4 colour 0 and ends in the position bytes of record 10.
Repeated $07 bytes at $9200–$920F, after the input consumed by the scene picture decode.
